04 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 4 February 1985, after the draft finalized by the Lubricants and Related Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 Cutting oils are intended for lubrication and cooling of metal surfaces during metal cutting operations. ` Neat ' cutting oils are to be distinguished from the ( soluble ' cutting oils in that the former are immiscible with water. The earlier version of this standard covered the sulphurized cutting oils for use with ferrous metals only. Cutting oils containing free dissolved sulphur would not be suitable for non-ferrous metals in view of the staining of the latter. Cutting oils intended for non-ferrous metals are mineral oils with or without added fatty oil; and the fatty oil may also be sulphurized in order to provide extreme pressure ( EP ) properties, but does not contain any free sulphur. In the revision of the standard the scope had been enlarged to cover all types of mat cutting oils intended both for ferrous and non-ferrous metals. The types covered were: a) irype 1 - mineral oil without added sulphur, having depending on the addition of fatty oil and intended machining of mild steel brass and light alloys. two grades for general

b)

Type 2 - mineral oil blended with sulphurized fatty oils which is non-staining and intended for use with non-ferrous metals and with two grades depending on the viscosity. Type 3 - sulphurred mineral oil which is staining use with ferrous metals and alloys. and intend for

c)

0.3 The present revision has been prepared as a result of a review of the standard by an Ad-hoc study group specially set up for this purpose as well as by the concerned technical committee in the light of the current

3

IS:

3065-

1985

requirements of neat cutting oils and the advancement in the lubrication In this revision, the various requirements for technology in the country. cutting oils have been modified in order to reflect a better quality of the material currently being marketed in the country. The number of grades under the different types have also been increased to cover all the types/ grades of cutting oils presently available in the market. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : Z-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

lS I 3065 - 1985 5.2 Marking - The containers shall be marked with the name, type and grade of the material; name of the manufacturer; and trade-mark, if any and with the batch number.

5.2.1 Mark.

The containers

may also be marked with the ISI

Certification

The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of NOTE the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS.1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by 181 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
